questions.question: In an extensive-form game, a strategy profile $\sigma$, together with Nature's probabilities, gives every node $x$ a probability $\mathbb{P}_\sigma(x)$ that play passes through it. What is the path of play of $\sigma$?
options: The nodes and actions reached with positive probability under $\sigma$
The branch from the root to the terminal node with the largest total payoff
The nodes at which every player's prescribed action is optimal
All decision nodes at which $\sigma$ prescribes an action for some player

questions.question: In the entry game, an entrant chooses Out, giving payoffs $(0,2)$ to (entrant, incumbent), or In; after In the incumbent chooses Accommodate ($A$), giving $(1,1)$, or Fight ($F$), giving $(-1,-1)$. Both (Out, $F$) and (In, $A$) are Nash equilibria. Is the incumbent's decision node on or off the equilibrium path?
options: Always off, since the incumbent moves only after the entrant has moved
It depends on the profile: off under (Out, $F$), on under (In, $A$)
Always on, since it is a decision node of the game tree
Off under (In, $A$) and on under (Out, $F$), where her threat matters

questions.question: In a Nash equilibrium $\sigma^*$ of an extensive-form game, a player may prescribe, at one of her information sets off the path of $\sigma^*$, an action she would never want to take if that set were reached. Why does the Nash condition allow this?
options: Off-path information sets belong to Nature, so the players choose nothing there
The Nash condition requires optimal actions everywhere, but only for the first mover
At an off-path set she cannot tell which node she is at, so no action can be compared
The set is never reached under $\sigma^*$, so that action leaves her payoff unchanged

questions.question: In the entry game, an entrant chooses Out, giving payoffs $(0,2)$ to (entrant, incumbent), or In; after In the incumbent chooses Accommodate ($A$), giving $(1,1)$, or Fight ($F$), giving $(-1,-1)$. Which nodes lie on the path of the Nash equilibrium (Out, $F$)?
options: Every node of the tree, since each player's action is specified
The root, the terminal node after Out and the incumbent's node
Only the root and the terminal node after Out
The root, the incumbent's node and the terminal node after $F$

questions.question: In the entry game, an entrant chooses Out, giving payoffs $(0,2)$ to (entrant, incumbent), or In; after In the incumbent chooses Accommodate ($A$), giving $(1,1)$, or Fight ($F$), giving $(-1,-1)$. Starting from the Nash equilibrium (Out, $F$), the incumbent alone changes her strategy from $F$ to $A$, and the entrant still plays Out. What are the new path and payoffs?
options: Path Out; payoffs $(0,2)$
Path In, then $A$; payoffs $(1,1)$
Path Out; payoffs $(1,1)$
Path Out, then $A$; payoffs $(0,1)$

questions.question: In sequential Battle of the Sexes, player 1 chooses $O$ or $F$; player 2 observes it and chooses $O$ or $F$. Matching at $O$ pays $(2,1)$, at $F$ $(1,2)$, a mismatch $(0,0)$; player 2's strategy lists her reply to $O$, then to $F$. For the Nash equilibrium $(F,FF)$, what are the path and payoffs, and which of player 2's planned replies is off the path?
options: Path $O$ then $F$, payoffs $(0,0)$; none of her replies is off the path
Path $F$ then $F$, payoffs $(1,2)$; her reply $F$ to $O$ is off the path
Path $F$ then $F$, payoffs $(1,2)$; her reply $F$ to $F$ is off the path
Path $F$ then $F$, payoffs $(2,1)$; her reply $F$ to $O$ is off the path

questions.question: In sequential Battle of the Sexes, player 1 chooses $O$ or $F$; player 2 observes it and chooses $O$ or $F$. Matching at $O$ pays $(2,1)$, at $F$ $(1,2)$, a mismatch $(0,0)$; player 2's strategy lists her reply to $O$, then to $F$. Its subgames are the whole game and the two starting at player 2's nodes. Under $(O,OF)$, which subgames are off the path?
options: One: the subgame after $F$
None: every subgame is on the path
Two: both subgames at player 2's nodes
One: the subgame after $O$

questions.question: Two pure-strategy profiles $\sigma$ and $\sigma'$ of an extensive-form game without moves of Nature induce the same path of play. $\sigma$ is subgame perfect (a Nash equilibrium in every subgame) and $\sigma'$ is a Nash equilibrium. What follows about $\sigma'$?
options: $\sigma'$ gives at least one player a different payoff from $\sigma$
$\sigma'$ is subgame perfect too, because payoffs depend only on the path
Same payoffs as $\sigma$; whether $\sigma'$ is subgame perfect is left open
$\sigma'$ is not subgame perfect, since a path belongs to one profile only

questions.question: To check whether a Nash equilibrium $\sigma^*$ of an extensive-form game is subgame perfect, that is, induces a Nash equilibrium in every subgame, which subgames still need to be examined?
options: Only those on the path, since off-path behaviour never affects any payoff
Only those off the path of $\sigma^*$; on-path ones pass automatically
Only the whole game, since $\sigma^*$ is already a Nash equilibrium there
Only the smallest subgames at the end of the tree, as in backward induction

questions.question: $\sigma^*$ is a Nash equilibrium of an extensive-form game. Player 2 changes her action at one of her information sets that is off the path of $\sigma^*$, and nothing else changes; call the new profile $\sigma'$. Which statement about $\sigma'$ is correct?
options: Its path changes, because player 2's new action is now carried out
Same path and payoffs, yet it may no longer be a Nash equilibrium
Player 2's payoff changes, while every other player's payoff stays the same
Same path and payoffs, so it is again a Nash equilibrium

questions.question: In an entry game the entrant chooses Out, giving (entrant, incumbent) $(0,2)$, or In; after In the incumbent accommodates, $(2,1)$, or fights, $(-1,-1)$. The incumbent fights with probability $r$. For which $r$ is (Out, fight with probability $r$) a Nash equilibrium with path Out?
options: $r\ge\tfrac{2}{3}$
Only $r=1$
$r\ge\tfrac{1}{2}$

questions.question: In sequential Battle of the Sexes, player 1 chooses $O$ or $F$; player 2 observes it and chooses $O$ or $F$. Matching at $O$ pays $(2,1)$, at $F$ $(1,2)$, a mismatch $(0,0)$; player 2's strategy lists her reply to $O$, then to $F$. For which strategies $s_2$ of player 2 is $(O,s_2)$ a Nash equilibrium?
options: All four strategies
Only $OF$
$OO$ and $OF$
$OO$, $OF$ and $FO$

questions.question: In the entry game the entrant chooses Out, which ends the game, or In, after which the incumbent chooses Accommodate or Fight. The entrant plays In with probability $0.4$ and the incumbent fights with probability $0.5$ (not necessarily an equilibrium). What is the probability of reaching the terminal node after Fight, and is the incumbent's node on the path?
options: $0.2$; off the path, since Out is more likely than In
$0.5$; on the path, as it is reached with probability $0.4$
$0.3$; on the path, as it is reached with probability $0.6$
$0.2$; on the path, as it is reached with probability $0.4$

questions.question: In a Nash equilibrium $\sigma^*$, player 2 has an information set $h=\{x,y\}$ with $\mathbb{P}_{\sigma^*}(x)=0$ and $\mathbb{P}_{\sigma^*}(y)=0.3$, where $h$ is on the path if $\mathbb{P}(x)+\mathbb{P}(y)>0$. Must her action at $h$ be optimal given these probabilities?
options: No: the Nash condition binds only at singleton information sets on the path
Yes: $h$ is on the path, and her action affects her payoff via $y$
Only at $y$; at $x$ she may choose a different action from the one at $y$
No: $x$ has probability $0$, so $h$ as a whole counts as off the path

questions.question: In a finite extensive-form game, Nature (if it moves) gives every action positive probability, and every player uses a behavioural strategy that puts positive probability on every action at each of her information sets. Which information sets are off the path?
options: Those that are not on the single most likely branch from the root
Those at which some action has probability below $\tfrac{1}{2}$
None: every node is reached with a product of positive probabilities
Those of the last mover, since play may end before she ever moves

questions.question: Player 1 chooses Out, giving $(1,3)$, or $L$ or $R$. Player 2 sees only that Out was not chosen, so her two nodes form one information set, where she picks $u$ or $d$: $(L,u)=(2,1)$, $(R,d)=(0,1)$, $(L,d)=(R,u)=(0,0)$. Is the Nash equilibrium (Out, $d$) subgame perfect, that is, a Nash equilibrium in every subgame?
options: Yes: the only subgame is the whole game, where it is a Nash equilibrium
No: the node after $L$ starts a subgame, and there $d$ gives player 2 $0<1$
No: player 2's off-path information set must be checked as a separate subgame
No: it is not even a Nash equilibrium, as $u$ is better after $L$

questions.question: Player 1 chooses Stop, giving $(1,1)$, or Continue; then player 2 chooses $l$, giving $(0,2)$, or $r$; after $r$ player 1 chooses $a$, giving $(3,0)$, or $b$, giving $(-1,-1)$. Is the profile where player 1 plays (Stop, $b$) and player 2 plays $l$ a Nash equilibrium?
options: Yes, and it is subgame perfect, since own off-path actions are never checked
No: player 1 could switch to (Continue, $a$) and earn $3$ instead of $1$
No: after $r$, $a$ gives player 1 $3>-1$, so $b$ violates the Nash conditions
Yes: with player 2 choosing $l$, no strategy gives player 1 more than $1$

questions.question: In a finite extensive-form game without moves of Nature, each player uses a pure strategy. What does the path of play of this profile look like?
options: One branch from the root for each player's chosen strategy
Every terminal node that can be reached from the root
The root plus every node at which an action is prescribed
One sequence of nodes from the root to a terminal node
